laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: IN Code §9-21-8-59 — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Handheld device use while driving is banned.
laws.penalty: $500 fine.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: all handheld device use while driving is banned since 2020.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §14-22-11-2 — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Indiana hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $18; hunting licenses cost approximately $24. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class A misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $500 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Indiana is a Class A misdemeanor with fines up to $500.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §9-30-5-1 — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $500–$5,000 fine, 90-day license suspension, up to 1 year jail. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Indiana for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Indiana is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §7.1-5-7-7 — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $500 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §35-48-4-11 — Recreational cannabis NOT legal
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Indiana. Possession of under 30g is a Class B misdemeanor. Indiana has no medical cannabis program either.
laws.penalty: Possession up to 30g: Class B misdemeanor. Larger amounts: felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana has no cannabis program — recreational and medical both illegal.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §35-48-4-11 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Indiana has no medical cannabis program — Indiana is one of the few remaining states without legal medical cannabis.
laws.penalty: Any cannabis: criminal offense.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Indiana does not have a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Constitutional
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §35-47-2-3 — Constitutional state
laws.fullDescription: Indiana is a constitutional state. Indiana enacted constitutional carry in 2022 (HEA 1296) — no permit required to carry a handgun for eligible adults.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: felony.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Indiana have?
quiz.explanation: Indiana has constitutional — permitless carry since 2022 for eligible adults

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Indiana require a federal NICS background check. Indiana does not require background checks for private gun sales.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Indiana require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Indiana only requires background checks for licensed dealer gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §35-41-3-2 — Stand Your Ground
laws.fullDescription: Indiana has a Stand Your Ground law — no duty to retreat before using force in self-defense.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a Stand Your Ground law?
options: No — duty to retreat outside home
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana has Stand Your Ground — no duty to retreat.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — $7.25/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Indiana's minimum wage is $7.25/hour (2024). Indiana uses the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hr.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped workers may have a lower base wage.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's minimum wage is $7.25/hour.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Indiana follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.
laws.penalty: N/A — at-will is the default standard.
laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Indiana employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Indiana is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — Yes
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Indiana is a right-to-work state
laws.fullDescription: Indiana is a right-to-work state. Indiana is a right-to-work state (since 2012).
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs labor relations framework.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees and some categories are governed by federal law.

quiz.q: Is Indiana a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Indiana is a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Business Code — Non-compete enforceability rules
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Non-compete agreements enforced if reasonable in scope and duration.
laws.penalty: Overly broad agreements may be voided or reformed by courts.
laws.exceptions: Agreements protecting legitimate trade secrets are most favored.

quiz.q: Are non-compete agreements automatically enforceable in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Courts assess reasonableness of non-competes.

laws.title: Paid Sick Leave — Not Required
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — No statewide mandate
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana has no statewide paid sick leave requirement.
laws.penalty: N/A
laws.exceptions: Independent contractors are generally not covered.

quiz.q: Does Indiana require employers to provide paid sick leave?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: No paid sick leave mandate in Indiana.

laws.title: Unemployment Insurance
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Unemployment benefits
laws.fullDescription: Indiana unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $390 for up to 26 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1500 in the base period.
laws.penalty: Filing fraudulent claims: repayment plus penalties and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Self-employed and independent contractors are generally ineligible for regular UI.

quiz.q: What is the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's maximum weekly unemployment benefit is $390.

laws.title: Workers' Compensation
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Mandatory workers' comp coverage
laws.fullDescription: Indiana requires employers with 1 or more employees to carry workers' compensation insurance. Covers medical costs and lost wages for work-related injuries.
laws.penalty: Employers without coverage: fines up to $5000/day, personal liability for claims.
laws.exceptions: Sole proprietors and some domestic workers may be exempt.

quiz.q: How many employees trigger workers' comp requirements in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana requires workers' comp for employers with 1 or more employees.

laws.title: Independent Contractor Classification
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Worker classification rules
laws.fullDescription: Indiana uses Common law control test to classify workers. Worker classification uses the common law control test.
laws.penalty: Misclassification: back taxes, penalties, and retroactive benefits liability.
laws.exceptions: Licensed professionals may have different classification standards.

quiz.q: What test does Indiana use for worker classification?
quiz.explanation: Indiana uses the Common law control test for worker classification.

laws.title: Child Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Labor Code — Restrictions on youth employment
laws.fullDescription: Indiana restricts employment of minors. Children under 14: very limited jobs only. Ages 14–15: restricted hours. Most minors under 18 need work permits. Federal child labor protections apply with state additions.
laws.penalty: Employers violating child labor laws: fines up to $10000 per violation.
laws.exceptions: Family farms and limited entertainment work have exemptions.

quiz.q: At what age do minors generally need work permits in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Most Indiana minors under 18 need work permits for regular employment.

laws.title: Equal Pay Act
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Civil Rights Code — Equal pay for equal work
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits pay discrimination based on sex for substantially equal work. Equal pay laws prohibit sex-based wage discrimination.
laws.penalty: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees for violations.
laws.exceptions: Pay differences justified by seniority, merit, or non-sex factors are permitted.

quiz.q: What agency enforces equal pay laws in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's civil rights agency and the federal EEOC both enforce equal pay laws.

laws.title: Anti-Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Civil Rights Code — Protected classes in Indiana
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits employment discrimination based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age (40+), and disability. Standard protected classes under state civil rights law.
laws.penalty: Compensatory damages, back pay, reinstatement, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Religious organizations may have limited exemptions for certain positions.

quiz.q: How many employees must an Indiana employer have before anti-discrimination laws apply?
quiz.explanation: Indiana anti-discrimination laws apply to employers with 15 or more employees.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice Requirement
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — 24-hour notice required
laws.fullDescription: Indiana landlords must give tenants 24 hours' written notice before entering for non-emergency purposes. Entry must be at reasonable times.
laws.penalty: Unlawful entry may entitle tenant to damages or lease termination.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies (fire, flood, imminent harm) allow immediate entry without notice.

quiz.q: How many hours notice must Indiana landlords give before entering?
quiz.explanation: Indiana landlords must give 24 hours' notice before non-emergency entry.

laws.title: Security Deposit Rules
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — Two months' rent maximum deposit
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Maximum security deposit is Two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized statement of deductions.
laws.penalty: Landlord who wrongfully withholds deposit may owe double damages plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits for pets may be separate in some cases.

quiz.q: How many days does a Indiana landlord have to return a security deposit?
quiz.explanation: Indiana landlords have 30 days to return security deposits after move-out.

laws.title: Rent Control Status — Not Statewide
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Housing Code — No statewide rent control
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana law preempts local rent control ordinances.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/regulatory matter.
laws.exceptions: Federally subsidized housing has separate rent rules.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have statewide rent control?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana prohibits local rent control.

laws.title: Eviction Process & Tenant Protections
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — Notice and court process required
laws.fullDescription: Indiana landlords must provide: 5 days notice for nonpayment; 10 days for violations; 30 days for no-cause termination. Court filing required after notice expires.
laws.penalty: Self-help eviction (changing locks, removing belongings) is illegal.
laws.exceptions: Emergency situations may allow expedited proceedings.

quiz.q: How many days notice for non-payment of rent before eviction in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana requires 5 days notice for nonpayment of rent before filing for eviction.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulations
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Regulated locally
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: STR regulations vary by municipality.
laws.penalty: Operating without required licenses: fines and possible closure.
laws.exceptions: Owner-occupied properties renting a single room may have reduced requirements.

quiz.q: Are short-term rentals (Airbnb) regulated in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana regulates STRs primarily at the local level with varying requirements by city.

laws.title: Property Tax
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Average 0.85% effective rate
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.85%. Indiana has a 1% cap on residential property tax rates, keeping effective rates modest.
laws.penalty: Delinquent taxes accrue interest and may result in tax lien or foreclosure.
laws.exceptions: Senior citizens and disabled veterans often receive exemptions. Senior and veteran exemptions available.

quiz.q: What is the approximate average effective property tax rate in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.85%.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §6-1.1-12-37 — $45,000 assessed value deduction homestead exemption
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana's homestead deduction reduces assessed value by $45,000 for primary residences. Additional deductions available for seniors.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protection for homeowners.
laws.exceptions: Does not protect against tax liens, mortgage foreclosures, or mechanic's liens.

quiz.q: What is Indiana's homestead exemption?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's homestead exemption is $45,000 assessed value deduction.

laws.title: State Income Tax — Yes — flat 3.05%
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §6-3-2-1 — Yes — flat 3.05%
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana has a flat state income tax of 3.05% (2024), one of the lowest flat rates in the US. Many counties also levy local income taxes.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties, back taxes, and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Federal income taxes apply to all residents regardless of state income tax.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana has a flat 3.05% state income tax plus local county taxes.

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Revenue Code — 7.0% statewide sales tax
laws.fullDescription: Indiana has a 7.0% statewide sales tax. Indiana has a high statewide sales tax of 7%, with no local add-ons, making the combined rate uniformly 7%. Combined state and local rates average 7.0%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties and criminal charges for substantial violations.
laws.exceptions: Exempt items typically include: Prescription drugs and groceries..

quiz.q: What is the statewide sales tax rate in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's statewide sales tax is 7.0%.

laws.title: Estate / Inheritance Tax — No
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Revenue Code — No state estate tax
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana repealed its inheritance tax in 2013.
laws.penalty: N/A — federal estate tax applies to all US residents with large estates.
laws.exceptions: Federal estate tax applies to estates over $13 million (2024).

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a state estate or inheritance tax?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana has no estate or inheritance tax.

laws.title: Smoke-Free Workplace Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Health Code — Clean Air Act / Smoke-Free law
laws.fullDescription: Indiana prohibits smoking in enclosed workplaces, restaurants, and bars.
laws.penalty: Violation: $100–$500 per incident for individuals.
laws.exceptions: Some private clubs and outdoor areas may be exempt.

quiz.q: Is smoking banned in workplaces and restaurants in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Comprehensive smoke-free law covers most indoor workplaces.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §9-19-7-1 — Helmets required for riders under 18
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana requires helmets for motorcycle riders under 18. Adults may ride without helmets.
laws.penalty: Helmet violation: $100 fine.
laws.exceptions: Adults 18+ are exempt from helmet requirements.

quiz.q: Who must wear a motorcycle helmet in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana only requires helmets for motorcycle riders under 18.

laws.title: Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Vehicle Code — Mandatory seatbelts
laws.fullDescription: Indiana requires all front-seat occupants to wear seatbelts. Children under 8 or under 60 lbs must be in child safety seats.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for violations; higher for child restraint violations.
laws.exceptions: Some commercial vehicles and emergency situations may have limited exemptions.

quiz.q: Is the seatbelt law a primary offense in Indiana?
options: Yes, police can stop for seatbelt alone
quiz.explanation: Indiana's seatbelt law is a primary enforcement offense.

laws.title: Speed Limits
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Vehicle Code — Statutory speed limits
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Residential: 25 mph; highways: 65 mph; interstates: 70 mph; school zones: 20 mph. Posted limits vary.
laws.penalty: Speeding fines start at $50 and increase with severity; reckless driving is a criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt when responding.

quiz.q: What is the interstate speed limit in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's standard interstate speed limit is 70 mph.

laws.title: Texting While Driving
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Vehicle Code — Texting while driving banned
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Texting while driving is prohibited.
laws.penalty: First offense: $500; repeat: $500.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are permitted while driving.

quiz.q: Is texting while driving banned in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana banned all handheld device use while driving in 2020 — $500 fine.

laws.title: DUI Checkpoint Legality
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Vehicle Code — Sobriety checkpoints permitted
laws.fullDescription: DUI sobriety checkpoints are legal in Indiana. DUI checkpoints legal with proper procedures.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines when checkpoints are legal.
laws.exceptions: Checkpoints must follow established procedures to be constitutional.

quiz.q: Are DUI sobriety checkpoints legal in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: DUI checkpoints are legal with proper procedures.

laws.title: Move Over Law
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Vehicle Code — Slow or move over for emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Indiana's Move Over Law requires drivers to change lanes or slow down when passing stopped emergency vehicles and tow trucks and highway maintenance vehicles with flashing lights on the roadway or shoulder.
laws.penalty: Violation: $250 fine; if injury or death results, criminal charges may apply.
laws.exceptions: Required only when safe to do so without creating greater hazard.

quiz.q: Does Indiana's Move Over Law cover tow trucks?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's Move Over Law covers tow trucks.

laws.title: Cell Phone Use While Driving
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §9-21-8-59 — Handheld device restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Beyond texting, Indiana restricts handheld phone use while driving.
laws.penalty: Fines range from $500 to $200.
laws.exceptions: Hands-free calls and navigation use are generally permitted.

quiz.q: Can drivers make calls on a handheld phone while driving in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Handheld phone restrictions apply while driving.

laws.title: Age of Majority
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Civil Code — Age 18 is legal adulthood
laws.fullDescription: In Indiana, the age of majority is 18. At 18, residents gain the right to vote, enter contracts, and make their own legal decisions. Age-specific restrictions still apply.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines civil rights.
laws.exceptions: Some rights have higher age thresholds: alcohol (21), cannabis where legal (21).

quiz.q: What is the age of majority in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's age of majority is 18, consistent with most US states.

laws.title: Voting Rights & Restoration
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Election Code — Voter eligibility and felon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Felons lose voting rights during incarceration; restoration rules vary by state.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible (while incarcerated): criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Mentally incapacitated persons adjudicated incompetent may lose voting rights.

quiz.q: When are voting rights restored to a felon in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Voting rights restored after completing sentence.

laws.title: Jury Duty Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Court Rules — Jury service
laws.fullDescription: Indiana citizens who are US citizens, 18+, registered voters (or driver's license holders) may be called for jury duty. Jurors receive $50/day. Employers must allow employees to serve.
laws.penalty: Willfully ignoring a jury summons: contempt of court, fines up to $500.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions include active military, police, extreme hardship, and some medical conditions.

quiz.q: What is the daily pay for jurors in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana jurors receive $50 per day for service.

laws.title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Child Welfare Act — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Designated professionals are mandatory reporters. Reports must be made to child protective services or law enforcement. Good-faith reporters are protected from liability.
laws.penalty: Failure to report known child abuse: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege may apply in limited circumstances.

quiz.q: Who must report suspected child abuse in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Designated professionals must report suspected child abuse.

laws.title: Age of Consent
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Criminal Code — Age of consent is 16
laws.fullDescription: Indiana's age of consent is 16. Sexual activity with persons under the age of consent is a criminal offense. Sex offenders must register with the state registry.
laws.penalty: Sexual abuse of a minor: Felony with sex offender registration..
laws.exceptions: Romeo and Juliet provision: Romeo and Juliet provision may apply for close-in-age couples..

quiz.q: What is the age of consent in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana's age of consent is 16.

laws.title: Emancipation of Minors
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Family Code — Court-ordered emancipation
laws.fullDescription: Indiana allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation, granting adult legal status. The court considers whether it's in the minor's best interests and whether the minor can support themselves.
laws.penalty: N/A — emancipation is a civil court process.
laws.exceptions: Emancipation does not override minimum age laws for alcohol, cannabis, or voting.

quiz.q: At what minimum age can a minor petition for emancipation in Indiana?
quiz.explanation: Indiana allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation.

laws.title: Curfew Laws for Minors
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Local ordinances only
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: No statewide curfew; municipalities set their own rules.
laws.penalty: Curfew violation: minor taken into custody and released to parents; parents may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Minors with employment, parental supervision, or school activities are typically exempt.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a statewide youth curfew?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Curfews set locally.

laws.title: Corporal Punishment in Schools
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Education Code — Corporal punishment prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Corporal punishment is permitted in Indiana public schools, with the caveat that it must not be excessive or cruel.
laws.penalty: Educators using prohibited corporal punishment face administrative discipline and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Physical restraint to prevent imminent harm is permitted.

quiz.q: Is corporal punishment allowed in Indiana public schools?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Corporal punishment is legal in Indiana public schools.

laws.title: Homeschooling Regulations
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Education Code — Homeschooling requirements
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Families must notify the school district and cover required subjects.
laws.penalty: Failure to provide required education: mandatory enrollment in public school.
laws.exceptions: Some states have additional oversight or assessment requirements.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have strict homeschooling regulations?
quiz.explanation: Indiana has moderate-regulation homeschooling with moderate requirements with notification and required subjects.

laws.title: School Vaccination Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Health Code — Required vaccinations for school entry
laws.fullDescription: Indiana requires students to be vaccinated against standard childhood diseases for school entry. Standard vaccinations required for school entry.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated students without exemptions may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions available: medical and religious exemptions.

quiz.q: Can Indiana parents claim a philosophical exemption from school vaccinations?
quiz.explanation: Indiana vaccination exemptions: medical and religious exemptions.

laws.title: Abortion Laws
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §16-34-2-1 — Near-total ban with exceptions
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Indiana banned most abortions effective August 2022 (SB 1), with exceptions for the life of the mother, fatal fetal anomalies, rape, and incest. This was later enjoined by courts.
laws.penalty: Performing illegal abortion: Level 5 felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical emergencies to save the life of the mother are typically exempt.

quiz.q: What is the gestational limit on abortion in Indiana?
options: Banned with exceptions for life, anomalies, rape
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana's near-total abortion ban includes exceptions for the mother's life, fatal anomalies, rape, and incest.

laws.title: Death Penalty — Authorized
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §35-50-2-9 — Death penalty status
laws.fullDescription: Indiana has the death penalty. Indiana authorizes the death penalty for murder with aggravating circumstances.
laws.penalty: Death penalty crimes: Capital murder.
laws.exceptions: Federal death penalty may apply to federal crimes regardless of state law.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have the death penalty?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Indiana has the death penalty for capital murder.

laws.title: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID)
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Criminal Code — Assisted suicide illegal
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Medical aid in dying is not legal.
laws.penalty: Assisting a suicide is a felony.

quiz.q: Is medical aid in dying (assisted suicide) legal in Indiana?

laws.title: Drug Penalties (Non-Cannabis)

laws.fullDescription: Indiana controlled substance penalties: Drug penalties follow state scheduling.

quiz.q: Is simple drug possession a felony in Indiana?

laws.title: Asset Forfeiture Laws

laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Civil asset forfeiture permitted for drug crimes.

laws.title: Expungement & Record Sealing
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Criminal Code — Expungement availability
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Record sealing or expungement available for eligible offenses.

quiz.q: Can first-time non-violent offenders expunge their records in Indiana?

laws.title: Solitary Confinement Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Corrections Code — Restricted housing policies
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: DOC policies limit solitary confinement use.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs prison administration.
laws.exceptions: Extremely dangerous inmates may face longer restricted housing.

quiz.q: Has Indiana restricted the use of solitary confinement?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Limited reforms on solitary confinement.

laws.title: Private Prison Use
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Corrections Code — Private correctional facilities
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Some private facilities used.

quiz.q: Does Indiana use privately operated prisons?

laws.title: Police Body Camera Requirements
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Law Enforcement Code — Body camera law
laws.fullDescription: Indiana: Body camera policies vary by department.

quiz.q: Does Indiana have a statewide body camera law?
quiz.explanation: Indiana: Body camera policies vary by agency.

laws.title: Police Use-of-Force Policies
laws.subtitle: Ind. Code §Criminal Code — Justified use of force
laws.fullDescription: Indiana law: deadly force justified only when necessary to prevent death or serious injury.
